newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian PM says will not alter government.
newsitem.headline: Belgian PM says will not alter government.

text.p: Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said on Monday he had no plans to alter his government in the wake of a scandal involving one of the parties in the current centre-left coalition.
"There is not a single reason to reshuffle the government," Dehaene told reporters after a party leaders' meeting of his own Flemish Christian Democratic party CVP.

A scandal over bribes allegedly paid to the Francophone Socialist Party (PS) had piled pressure on Dehaene's government in recent weeks and sparked calls for the PS to leave the government and for the coalition to quit altogether.

Last week two former senior PS officials were arrested and later charged with corruption in connection with an investigation of a 1989 bribes-for-airforce-contracts affair implicating French defence firm Dassault.
Their lawyers said that on behalf of the PS the officials, both aides to senior party politicians, received 30 million francs (about $1 million) from Dassault.
A former Belgian army colonel, reportedly a lobbyist for Dassault, has also been charged with corruption.
